learning: Iterations 1 to 5 show the slalom fails at max_error 0.062 to 0.064 whatever the span, footprint, lead (0.04 or 0.06) or track width. Lead 0.04 m was clearly worse on the oval and s-bend, so a longer lead of 0.07 m is the one untested direction.
notes: Runnable package: iteration 5 geometry with the sensor lead changed from y=0.06 m to y=0.07 m. Weights, kp, kd, base_speed and line_loss are unchanged, so the lead is the only variable under test.
rationale: Iteration 5 is the best design so far (653.3). Its oval finished 20/20 at 1.85 s and its s-bend finished 18/20 with steering_oscillation 0.335, under the 0.35 limit. The slalom is still 0/20, with 1.0 line-loss events and max_error 0.0644. Across five variants (span, footprint, lead 0.04 m, wheel_track), the slalom has stayed at max_error 0.062 to 0.064. The Builder's intent changes only the sensor lead, from 0.06 m to 0.07 m, to test whether a longer look-ahead helps the slalom. I keep the iteration 5 geometry and controller exactly as the Builder specified: kp 3.6, kd 0.9, ki 0, weights -2 to +2 linear, base_speed 1.6, last_direction. Changing only the lead keeps the race a clean test of lead. The observation request covers max_error and line_loss_events for the slalom exit, and steering_oscillation on all tracks, because a longer lead may add s-bend jitter. Expected: slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.0 or max_error drops below 0.06, and the oval stays 20/20. No outcome is claimed for this package.
